title: Database Query Execution
summary: Build the iterator-model executor of a small relational database: scans, filters with NULL logic, projections, three join algorithms, an index scan, aggregation and a cost-based planner.
description: A query is a tree of operators and every row is pulled up through it one at a time. You build that executor in Go: table scans and filters with SQL's three-valued NULL logic, projection and limit, nested-loop, hash and sort-merge joins, a range index scan, grouping and aggregation, and finally a rule-based planner that picks between plans with a cost model. Tests compare your results with independent brute-force references and read work counters (rows read, opens, comparisons), never the clock, so a correct but wasteful operator fails and a fast machine can't hide it. NULLs and duplicate keys are the edge cases throughout.
outcomes: Explain and implement the iterator (pull) model of query execution.
Apply SQL three-valued logic correctly in filters, joins and aggregates.
Choose between scan, index, nested-loop, hash and merge strategies using a stated cost model and verify the choice with work counters.
